[[Southampton Airport]] | website = {{Official URL}} }} {{Location map many|United Kingdom||float=right|width=250|caption=The 3 airports owned by AGS| |label1=[[Aberdeen Airport|Aberdeen]]|pos1=right|lat1=57.201944|long1=-2.197778 |label2=[[Glasgow Airport|Glasgow]]|pos2=left|lat2=55.871944|long2=-4.433056 |label3=[[Southampton Airport|Southampton]]|pos3=left|lat3=50.950278|long3=-1.356667}} '''AGS Airports Limited''' is the owner of [[Aberdeen Airport|Aberdeen]], [[Glasgow Airport|Glasgow]] and [[Southampton Airport|Southampton]] airports. Based in [[Leeds]], England, it was formed in September 2014 by [[Ferrovial]] and [[Macquarie Group]]. In January 2025 it was sold to [[AviAlliance]]. ==History== [[Aberdeen Airport|Aberdeen]], [[Glasgow Airport|Glasgow]] and [[Southampton Airport|Southampton]] airports were originally owned and operated by the British Airports Authority, which acquired them in the 1970s. In the late 1980s the authority was sold off by the government and became BAA plc. By 2012 BAA had sold off three of its seven airports and rebranded as [[Heathrow Airport Holdings]] (HAH). In 2014 HAH decided to sell off Aberdeen, Glasgow and Southampton to enable the company to focus on improving Heathrow for passengers and winning support for Heathrow expansion.{{Cite web|title = Glasgow airport boss to become chief executive as buyout completed|url = http://www.heraldscotland.com/news/13194066.Glasgow_airport_boss_to_become_chief_executive_as_buyout_completed/|website =[[Glasgow Herald]]| date=18 December 2014 |location=Glasgow|accessdate = 2015-10-01}} Meanwhile, AGS Airports was formed by [[Ferrovial]] and [[Macquarie Group]]. In December 2014, three months after being incorporated, AGS acquired Aberdeen, Glasgow and Southampton Airports from HAH.[https://web.archive.org/web/20201202003815/https://www.macquarie.com/au/en/about/news/2014/ferrovial-and-macquarie-fund-acquire-aberdeen-glasgow-and-southamption-airports-for-gbp1048-million.html
